body.statement: Let \(\mathcal G\) be an ADMG on \(V\). If two subgraphs \(F,F'\) of \(\mathcal G\) form a hedge for \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\), then this causal effect is not identifiable from \(P(V)\) in \(\mathcal G\).

source.locator: Definition 16, p. 1950; Theorem 17 statement, p. 1951; proof, p. 1968
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 17 Let F,F′ be subgraphs of G which form a hedge for P(y|do(x)). Then P(v),G does not identify P(y|do(x)).

attestation.note: Verified by mill-w03 against the official JMLR 9 (2008) PDF: hedge definition on printed page 1950, statement on 1951, full proof on 1968, downloaded 2026-09-10. The symbolic non-identifiability turnstile is rendered here in words.
